instructions: Put the 8 dried shiitake in a bowl, cover them with boiling water and leave them for 30 minutes to soften.
Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a saucepan with 1 3/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Turn the heat to low, cover the pan and cook the rice for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you're ready to serve.

Meanwhile, make the marinade. Grate a quarter of the apple into a bowl, then mince 3 of the garlic cloves and grate the ginger (about 1 tsp) into it. Stir in 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, the 1 tbsp honey and 2 tsp of the sesame oil.
Slice the steak as thin as you can across the grain. Toss it in the marinade and leave it for about 30 minutes while you do the vegetables.
Cut the 2 carrots and the 2 zucchini into thin sticks about 2 inches long. Cut the spinach into 2 inch lengths. Mince 3 more garlic cloves for the vegetables.

Make the sauce. Finely grate the last garlic clove into a small bowl and stir in the 1/4 cup gochujang, 2 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 1/2 tsp of the soy sauce, 1 tbsp of the sugar and 2 tsp of the sesame oil, until the sugar dissolves.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Drain the mushrooms, squeeze out the water, cut off the stems and slice the caps.

Heat 2 tsp of the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium high. Cook the mushrooms for 2 minutes, stirring. Add the last 1 1/2 tsp soy sauce, the last 1/4 tsp sugar and a third of the minced vegetable garlic, stir for 1 minute, then transfer them onto a large plate.

Add 2 tsp of the vegetable oil to the same skillet with the carrots and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring, until they're tender but still have a little bite. Move them to the plate.
Add 2 tsp of the vegetable oil with the zucchini and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for about 4 minutes, stirring, until it's just tender. Move it to the plate.

Add 1 tsp of the vegetable oil and 1 tsp of the sesame oil, then the spinach. Toss it for about 1 minute until it wilts, then stir in another third of the vegetable garlic and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Transfer it into a strainer to cool.
Drop the bean sprouts into the boiling water and cook them for about 5 minutes, until they're floppy. Drain them and rinse them under cold water.

Squeeze as much water out of the sprouts as you can with your hands. Toss them in a bowl with 2 tsp of the sesame oil, the last of the vegetable garlic and the last 1/4 tsp salt. Squeeze the water out of the spinach too.

Wipe out the skillet and heat 2 tsp of the vegetable oil over high until it shimmers. Lift the beef out of the marinade, letting the extra drip off, and cook it for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until it's cooked through with some caramelized edges. Move it to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium and add the last 1 tbsp vegetable oil. Crack in the 4 eggs and fry them for 2 to 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny.
Taste a little of each vegetable. Add a pinch more salt to any that's flat.

Divide the rice among 4 bowls. Arrange the beef and each vegetable in its own pile on top, then put an egg in the middle. Sprinkle with the 2 tsp sesame seeds and drizzle with the last 2 tsp sesame oil.
Serve with the gochujang sauce on the side.
method_notes: All three versions top rice with separately cooked, separately seasoned vegetables and beef, add a fried egg and serve a gochujang sauce. RecipeTin Eats marinates the beef in soy, honey, grated apple, garlic and ginger, cooks each vegetable in turn in one skillet, and makes a sweet and tangy sauce with mirin and rice vinegar. Korean Bapsang blanches the sprouts and spinach, salts the cucumber, adds a spicy radish salad and keeps the sauce to gochujang, sugar and sesame oil, and Love and Lemons goes meat free with a smaller set of vegetables. This one follows the lead's marinade, vegetables and sauce, uses the lead's alternative of simmering the sprouts, and leaves the sauce on the side.
